edges.description: Multisystem lysosomal storage in craniofacial soft tissues and bone produces coarse facies.
The multisystem storage phenotype includes dysostosis multiplex and skeletal remodeling defects.
Defective glycoprotein catabolism and excessive lysosomal exocytosis in cartilage and bone cause generalized skeletal dysplasia.
Skeletal storage disease includes vertebral morphology abnormalities and deformities.
Visceral reticuloendothelial and parenchymal storage disease causes visceromegaly, prominent in early-onset disease.
Severe prenatal multisystem lysosomal storage and vascular/visceral dysfunction manifest in utero as fetal hydrops.
Severe early-onset multisystem storage and myocardial/valvular involvement lead to cardiac failure.
Severe early-onset systemic lysosomal storage in renal parenchyma causes progressive nephropathy and renal failure.
Neurologic storage disease is associated with intellectual disability.
Storage-related neurologic and otologic involvement includes hearing impairment.
Neurologic involvement in galactosialidosis includes seizures.
Ocular stromal storage involvement includes corneal opacity.
Recapitulates systemic early-onset pathology (nephropathy, splenomegaly, cardiac involvement) and acute progressive cerebellar ataxia driven by regional Purkinje cell loss.
Deficient cathepsin A esterase/carboxypeptidase activity directly reflects the primary CTSA defect and distinguishes galactosialidosis from isolated sialidosis or GM1 gangliosidosis.
Concurrent reduction of both NEU1 and GLB1 enzymatic activities in cells is the hallmark secondary biochemical signature of galactosialidosis.
edges.source: Secondary Combined NEU1 and GLB1 Deficiency
